introduction-the-problem-with-ephemeral-.core: A container's writable layer disappears when the container is replaced, and Pods move between nodes. Persistent data needs storage whose lifecycle is independent of Pods: Kubernetes models it with PersistentVolumes (the storage) and PersistentVolumeClaims (a request for it), provisioned through StorageClasses and CSI drivers.

first_principles.problem: A database Pod restarts on another node and comes back empty.
derivation: Use **CSI drivers** for real storage systems.

analogy.title: Hotel rooms versus a storage unit
analogy.story: Your stuff in the hotel room is cleared at checkout; the storage unit keeps it wherever you stay next.
analogy.breaks: Storage units are reachable from anywhere in town; many volumes are tied to one zone.

example.title: Data loss vs persistence
flow: Without PVC: data in container layer → lost on restart
With PVC: volume reattached → data intact

check.q: Where should a database Pod store its data in Kubernetes?
check.a: On a PersistentVolume via a PersistentVolumeClaim, not in the container's writable layer.

the-dynamic-duo-pv-and-pvc.core: A PersistentVolume is a cluster resource representing actual storage (size, access modes, backend). A PersistentVolumeClaim is a namespaced request (size, access mode, StorageClass). The control plane binds a PVC to a matching PV one-to-one, and Pods mount the PVC. Access modes are ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany and ReadWriteOncePod.

first_principles.problem: Developers shouldn't need to know which disk or NFS share backs their volume.
truths: Supply and demand can be separated.
Access modes depend on the backend.

analogy.title: A car rental desk
analogy.story: You request 'a large estate car'; the desk assigns a specific car from the fleet.
analogy.breaks: Rental cars are returned to a shared pool; PV reuse depends on the reclaim policy.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A 100 GiB gp3 volume is provisioned and bound.

code.text:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: data}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: gp3
  resources: {requests: {storage: 100Gi}}

check.q: Which access mode lets many nodes mount a volume read-write?

storageclasses-automating-the-magic.core: A StorageClass describes a type of storage (CSI provisioner, parameters such as volume type and IOPS, reclaim policy, expansion support, volumeBindingMode). PVCs naming a class trigger dynamic provisioning. WaitForFirstConsumer delays creation until a Pod is scheduled, so zonal volumes land in the Pod's zone.

first_principles.problem: Volumes are created in zone a while Pods are scheduled in zone b, leaving them unmountable.
truths: Zonal storage must match Pod placement.

analogy.title: A menu of storage options with a kitchen that cooks on order
analogy.story: Order 'fast SSD, 50 GB' and it's made fresh, delivered to your table's location.
analogy.breaks: Kitchens serve any table; zonal volumes can only serve Pods in the same zone.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Encrypted gp3 volumes in the Pod's zone, expandable.

code.text:
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: gp3}
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
parameters: {type: gp3, iops: "6000", throughput: "250", encrypted: "true"}
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
reclaimPolicy: Delete

check.a: So the volume is created in the zone where the Pod is scheduled, avoiding cross-zone mount failures.

reclaim-policies-what-happens-when-you-d.core: When a PVC is deleted, the bound PV's reclaimPolicy decides its fate: Delete removes the PV and the backing storage (the default for dynamic provisioning), Retain keeps the PV and data for manual recovery or reuse. StatefulSet PVC retention policies separately control whether PVCs are deleted on scale-down or StatefulSet deletion.

first_principles.problem: Deleting a namespace wipes a production database volume because the class used Delete.
truths: Deletion can cascade to real storage.

analogy.title: Cancelling a storage unit lease
analogy.story: Either the contents are thrown away, or the unit is locked and kept for you to collect.
analogy.breaks: Storage firms call you first; Kubernetes deletes instantly with Delete.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Deleting the PVC no longer destroys the disk.

check.q: What's the default reclaim policy for dynamically provisioned volumes?

the-plumbing-container-storage-interface.core: CSI is the standard interface between Kubernetes and storage systems. A CSI driver has a controller component (create, delete, attach, snapshot, expand volumes via the storage API) and a node component (DaemonSet that stages and mounts volumes on nodes). Sidecars (external-provisioner, attacher, resizer, snapshotter) translate Kubernetes objects into CSI calls.

first_principles.problem: Storage vendors once had to ship code inside Kubernetes itself (in-tree drivers), slowing everyone down.
derivation: Debug via **driver logs and VolumeAttachment** objects.

analogy.title: Universal plugs and adapters
analogy.story: Any appliance (storage) works with any socket (Kubernetes) through a standard adapter.
analogy.breaks: Plugs are passive; CSI drivers run active controllers and node agents.

steps.label: Finding
steps.detail: Attach timeout: volume still attached to old node.

code.text:
kubectl get volumeattachments
kubectl logs -n kube-system deploy/ebs-csi-controller -c csi-attacher
kubectl logs -n kube-system ds/ebs-csi-node -c ebs-plugin

check.q: Which CSI component mounts the volume on the node?
check.a: The node plugin (via NodeStage/NodePublish), usually a DaemonSet.

volume-snapshots-and-ephemeral-volumes.core: VolumeSnapshots (with VolumeSnapshotClass and CSI snapshotter) capture point-in-time copies of PVCs, and new PVCs can be restored from them (dataSource), or cloned from existing PVCs. Ephemeral volumes cover Pod-lifetime needs: emptyDir (optionally memory-backed), generic ephemeral volumes (a per-Pod PVC deleted with the Pod) and CSI ephemeral volumes.

first_principles.problem: A team needs consistent backups of database volumes and fast scratch space for batch jobs.
truths: Some data only lives as long as the Pod.
Scratch can need real disk performance.
derivation: Use **emptyDir** for scratch, **medium: Memory** for tmpfs.
Use **generic ephemeral volumes** for large per-Pod scratch.

analogy.title: Photos of a whiteboard and disposable notepads
analogy.story: Snapshots preserve the board; notepads are thrown away after the meeting.
analogy.breaks: Photos capture instantly; crash-consistent snapshots may need app quiescing for consistency.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Restored copy for testing or recovery.

check.q: How do you restore a PVC from a VolumeSnapshot?
check.a: Create a new PVC with dataSource pointing to the VolumeSnapshot.
